title: The tree-trunk mistake
myth: 550 billion tonnes of living carbon ÷ 3.1×10³⁰ cells = 177 femtograms per cell
why: 69% of living carbon is wood, which is mostly dead tissue with almost no living cells. Count cells only in the living compartments.
sources: Bar-On, Phillips & Milo 2018; Kallmeyer et al. 2012; Magnabosco et al. 2018

title: The onion test
myth: Every letter of DNA is an instruction
measured: 3.6×10³⁷ bits of DNA copies, but only ~3.8×10¹² unique bits (~475 GB)
why: An onion's genome is five times bigger than yours. Most DNA is copies of the same genes or filler that selection ignores, so copies, working DNA and unique code are counted separately.
sources: Graur et al. 2013; Lynch & Conery 2003; Landenmark, Forgan & Cockell 2015

title: RAM is not a hard drive
measured: 15 zettabytes installed; ~200 zettabytes a year is traffic that mostly isn't kept
why: Video streamed and thrown away is not storage. Short-lived working memory and long-term storage are kept apart, and no bit counts are invented where nobody measured them.
sources: IDC Global DataSphere and StorageSphere; Gagliano et al. 2014

title: The 3,100-terawatt paradox
measured: About 65 TW for all life on Earth
why: All photosynthesis on Earth captures only ~220–250 TW. Wild microbes mostly starve at a tiny fraction of lab rates, and the energy budget has to fit under that ceiling.
sources: Field et al. 1998; Kleidon 2010; Hoehler & Jørgensen 2013

title: The baboon-brained T. rex
myth: T. rex had over 3 billion forebrain neurons, like a baboon
measured: About 250–360 million, packed like a reptile's
why: Dinosaur braincases were only partly filled with brain. And humans hold only ~0.02% of Earth's neurons: tiny invertebrates hold most of them.
sources: Caspar et al. 2024; Herculano-Houzel 2016; Olkowicz et al. 2016

title: Marketing-peak computing
myth: The world's computers do 10²⁵–10²⁹ operations per second
measured: About 1.9×10²² operations per second actually executed
why: Peak chip ratings assume every device runs flat out all day. Real use is far lower. All silicon together does about 0.006% of the synaptic activity of the world's animals.
sources: Epoch AI 2025; IEA 2024; device shipment and utilization data

title: Clay outlives the SSD
myth: One half-life fits each storage medium
measured: Baked clay: ~3,500–5,000 years unpowered. An unplugged SSD: about a thousand times shorter.
why: Living lineages, buried fossils and human archives decay by different physics, so persistence is tracked three separate ways.
sources: JEDEC JESD218B; Allentoft et al. 2012; Schmandt-Besserat 1992

title: Independent error bars
myth: Each estimate's uncertainty can be added up separately
why: The cell count drives six other numbers, so they rise and fall together. Even at the extremes, silicon stays below 0.023% of animal synaptic activity.
sources: Joint Monte Carlo over shared drivers (10,000 draws, seed 42)
